## business-model / 11_capital-allocation-governance.md

_Source: `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md`_

# Capital Allocation & Governance — EMAR

*Emaar Properties PJSC (DFM: EMAAR) — UAE / Dubai Financial Market, IFRS, reporting currency AED, fiscal year ends 31 December. Filings are in English; no translation gap. Controlled anchor shareholder is the Government of Dubai (via ICD until May 2026, now Emirates Power Investment / Dubai Holding).*

## 1. Signal Table

Severity is INVERTED — **higher score = worse**.

| Signal | Observation | Evidence | Severity /100 *(higher = worse)* |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Acquisition pattern (frequency, size, integration; serial-acquirer + opportunity cost — Filter 4) | Growth is mainly organic mega-development (e.g. the AED 200bn masterplan announced Jun 2026), with recent M&A limited to consolidating its own affiliate (Emaar Malls minority buy-in, 2021) and one large related-party purchase — Dubai Creek Harbour bought from Dubai Holding for AED 7.5bn in Aug 2022, half cash / half Emaar shares — so it is not a debt-funded serial acquirer, though legacy 2005–2012 overseas deals (India/MGF, Egypt, Turkey) left impairments and live litigation. | [CIQ Direct Investments, snapshot 2026-06-28; CIQ Key Developments, Jun 2026; CIQ Financials_Annual › Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025] | 42 |
| Net share count trajectory (buybacks minus issuance, dilution) | Shares have been flat at 8,838.8m every quarter from Q4 2024 to Q1 2026 with no buybacks, after an earlier step-up funded by share-based deals (Emaar Malls swap 2021; Dubai Creek Harbour part-consideration to Dubai Holding 2022). | [CIQ Financials_Annual › Historical Capitalization, Q4 2024–Q1 2026; FY2025 AR (IFRS), EPS note — wtd-avg 8,838,790k; CIQ Direct Investments] | 32 |
| Dividend policy & coverage | Cash dividend held at AED 1.00/share (AED 8,838.8m) for FY2023–FY2025 — about 50% of FY2025 EPS of AED 1.99 and a small fraction of operating cash flow (AED 33.5bn), so cover is deep. | [FY2025 AR (IFRS), Note 32 (Dividends), p.212; CIQ Financials_Annual › Ratios (DPS); CIQ Financials_Annual › Cash Flow] | 15 |
| Capex intensity vs depreciation (growth vs maintenance) | Fixed-asset capex (AED 934m FY2025) runs below depreciation & amortisation (AED 1,685m) — normal for an off-plan developer whose growth capital goes into development inventory funded by customer advances, not fixed assets; a growing AED ~35bn project-commitment book is the real forward capital call. | [CIQ Financials_Annual › Cash Flow, FY2025; FY2025 AR, Note 31 (Commitments), p.212] | 22 |
| Debt level and trajectory (absolute + vs EBITDA) | Net cash of ~AED 25.0bn (broad basis, nets short-term investments) — total debt of only AED 10.06bn sits far below the AED 35.0bn cash-and-short-term-investment balance, Total Debt/EBITDA is 0.40x, EBITDA/interest is ~52x, and debt has fallen every year since 2021 (§24 Filter 3 positive). | [ciq_facts net_debt −24,969.2 / total_debt 10,064.4 / interest_coverage 52.1x, Q1 & LTM Mar-31-2026; CIQ Financials_Annual › Capital Structure Summary; CIQ › Ratios] | 12 |
| Related-party transactions | Disclosed RPT is small (cost of revenue AED 130m, finance cost AED 138m, KMP pay AED 129m — well under 1% of AED 49.6bn revenue), but under the IAS 24 government-related-entity exemption Emaar elects NOT to itemise the bulk of its dealings with the Dubai-Government / ICD ecosystem (land purchases, utilities, construction), which the AED 7.5bn Dubai Creek Harbour deal shows can be very large. | [FY2025 AR (IFRS), Note 33 (Related Party Disclosures), p.212; CIQ Direct Investments (Dubai Creek Harbour)] | 55 |
| Insider / promoter ownership and changes | Control rests with the Government of Dubai — the 22.27% anchor block was transferred in May 2026 from ICD to Emirates Power Investment (AED 23.9bn deal), lifting Dubai Holding group to 29.73%; individual insiders hold just 0.03%, and founder-MD Alabbar simultaneously chairs a competing private developer, Eagle Hills (§24 Filter 6 — unaligned/government owner). | [CIQ Public Ownership Summary, positions Dec-2025–May-2026; CIQ Key Developments, 2026-05-11; CIQ Board Members] | 50 |
| Promoter share pledging *(if applicable)* | Not applicable — a UAE/DFM issuer has no promoter-pledge regime, and no pledging of the Government/Dubai Holding stake is disclosed. | [Not applicable — UAE/DFM issuer] | 0 |
| Auditor history (changes, qualifications, KAMs) | Ernst & Young (Middle East, Dubai Branch) audits the parent, issued an unqualified FY2025 opinion and was re-appointed, with two standard real-estate Key Audit Matters (property-sale revenue recognition; net-realisable/recoverable value of development and investment properties) and no going-concern flag. | [FY2025 AR (IFRS), Independent Auditors' Report (EY Middle East) + Key Audit Matters] | 15 |
| Restatements / accounting policy changes | No material restatement or accounting-policy red flag; CIQ tags FY2021 as restated (RS) with later years original/normal, consistent with routine IFRS presentation. | [CIQ Financials_Annual › Cash Flow, Restatement Type row; FY2025 AR, basis of preparation] | 15 |
| Off-balance-sheet items | Off-balance-sheet exposure is disclosed and contained — RERA project performance guarantees AED 9.0bn (regulatory escrow), AED 130.7m share of associate/JV contingent liabilities, and legacy Emaar-India litigation (peak exposure ~AED 0.6bn) — with no hidden financing vehicles. | [FY2025 AR (IFRS), Note 30 (Guarantees & Contingencies), p.210–211; Note 31 (Commitments)] | 30 |
| Working capital trend (receivable days, inventory days, cash conversion) | The cash-conversion cycle is long but structurally explained by multi-year off-plan installment receivables, and it has improved steadily from ~660 days (2022) to ~370 days (LTM) while customer advances (unearned revenue, +AED 8.2bn in FY2025) self-fund construction. | [CIQ Financials_Annual › Ratios (Days Sales/Inventory/Payable Out., Cash Conversion Cycle); CIQ › Cash Flow (Change in Unearned Rev.)] | 22 |
| Senior management turnover (CEO, CFO, board chair in last 3 years) | Group Head of Finance changed in May 2026 (Hesham Heikal out 20-May, Pawan Chindalia in from Emaar Development), and the board was refreshed in 2024–2025 with several Dubai-Government / Dubai Holding appointees, while founder-MD Alabbar and Chairman Bin Thaniah (both since Dec 2020) stayed in place. | [CIQ Key Developments, 2026-05-22 (CFO change); CIQ Board Members, tenure fields] | 40 |

## 2. Classification

**Standard professional management** — with explicit government-control governance caveats.

On the capital-allocation axis the record is clean and repeatable: net cash of ~AED 25bn with debt falling every year, a dividend held at AED 1.00/share and covered ~2x by earnings and far more by cash flow, no buyback-vs-dilution games (share count flat since 2021), an unqualified EY audit, no material restatement, and working capital that self-funds via customer advances. It is not "owner-operator discipline" — insiders hold 0.03%, the controller is the state, and the founder-MD runs a competing developer — and it is not "capital allocation concerns," because there is no overpaid debt-funded M&A spree or runaway capex. It is also short of "governance red flags" in the critical sense: no auditor churn, no going-concern, disclosed related-party dealings are under 1% of revenue. What keeps it out of a cleaner bucket is a cluster of structural, ownership-driven features typical of a state-controlled entity — thin board independence (2 of ~11 directors independent; non-independent Chairman, Vice-Chairman and MD), and the IAS 24 election to leave the bulk of Dubai-Government-ecosystem transactions unquantified.

## 3. Most Material Signal

The related-party / controlling-owner cluster (severity 55/50). Emaar is anchored by the Government of Dubai, whose block moved in May 2026 from ICD to Emirates Power Investment / Dubai Holding (group stake now 29.73%), and management uses the IAS 24 government-related-entity exemption to *not* itemise its financing, land-purchase, utility and construction dealings with that ecosystem — the very channel through which the AED 7.5bn Dubai Creek Harbour asset was bought from Dubai Holding (part-funded by issuing Emaar shares to the same parent). Today that channel is not visibly extractive: dividends flow pro-rata to all holders, returns on capital are rising (ROCE ~4.7%→13.7% over five years), and the balance sheet is net cash. But it is the signal that, if it deteriorated — another large asset bought from the parent at a rich price, fresh dilution to fund it, or a swing from net-cash toward funding state projects — would move the classification to "Governance red flags." It is unquantifiable to a minority holder by construction, which is exactly why it is the one to watch.

## 4. Capital Allocation Score /100

**66 / 100** *(higher = better — better discipline, cleaner governance)*

The score reflects genuinely conservative balance-sheet and distribution behaviour (net cash, ~0.40x Total Debt/EBITDA, ~52x interest cover, a covered and steady dividend, flat share count, clean unqualified audit, improving cash conversion), marked down for the standing governance features of a Dubai-Government-controlled issuer: thin board independence, a founder-MD with a competing private vehicle, and — the biggest single deduction — the IAS 24 election that leaves most government-ecosystem related-party activity undisclosed. It sits in the lower half of the "strong / low-risk" band rather than higher precisely because the capital-allocation discipline is real but the minority-alignment picture is not.

**Rejector-filter cap (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4):** NOT applied. The acquisition-pattern row scored 42 (< 70). Emaar is not a serial acquirer — its capital engine is organic development, its two recent deals were affiliate/related-party consolidations rather than debt-funded third-party roll-ups, and it carries net cash rather than acquisition debt near or above its own value. The separate Filter 6 concern (unaligned government owner) is surfaced in the ownership and related-party rows and flagged as the most material signal; it is a structural caution carried to synthesis and the valuation layer, not a Filter-4 capital-allocation cap.

## business-model / 12_red-flags-sweep.md

_Source: `business-model/12_red-flags-sweep.md`_

# Red Flags Sweep — EMAR

*Emaar Properties PJSC (DFM: EMAAR). Dubai/UAE master-planned real-estate developer; IFRS, reporting currency AED (dirham, pegged to the US dollar at ~3.6725); fiscal year = calendar year. Latest audited year FY2025 (ended 31 Dec 2025); latest quarter Q1 2026. Filings are in English — no translation gap, and a home-language disclosure would not be treated as opacity (CLAUDE.md §27). All six upstream specialist outputs were present; no degraded-confidence note needed.*

This sweep is the catch-all: it surfaces only evidence-backed items that upstream specialists did **not** already make prominent. It does not re-score the moat, re-rate quality, or reach a verdict.

## 1. Already Covered Upstream

Listed so the synthesizer can see these are **not** re-flagged below.

| Upstream Agent | Flag Already Surfaced |

| disqualifier-scan | No disqualifier tripped. Clean/unqualified audits FY2023–25, no going-concern; no share pledge (only PP&E asset security); RPT 0.35% of revenue / 1.2% of expenses with the IAS 24 government-related-entity **non-disclosure caveat**; one disclosed auditor rotation (KPMG→EY); no material restatement; no financial-reporting enforcement; **India Enforcement Directorate / land contingency** (AED 190m attached, ~0.2% of assets); positive operating cash flow every year. Soft signals routed: government/unaligned-owner control, RP-transparency, CFO (Group Head of Finance) change. |
| segment-map | Three IFRS-8 segments; **Real Estate 80% of revenue / 75% of segment profit** (dominant, cyclical); Real Estate margin **flattered by ~AED 2.77bn finance income**; recurring Leasing/Retail is the ~69%-margin annuity; single-city (Dubai) concentration; segment disclosure granular. |
| customer-geography | No single-customer concentration (large granular buyer base, 0.5% default rate); **geography concentration extreme and rising — UAE/Dubai 93% of revenue**; 97% of receivables from MENA; AED 155bn backlog secures ~4 years near-term. |
| business-quality | Aggregate 53/100. **Cyclicality (27) is the defining risk**; pricing power/margins/ROIC are **cycle-flattered by legacy cheap land** (through-cycle ROIC ~8–10% vs LTM 13.7%); new land now bought at market prices (AED 120bn GDV in 2025); **FY2025 tax cushioned by a one-off relief**; not a technology-disruption bet (§24 Filter 5 not tripped). |

| capital-allocation-governance | 66/100. Net cash ~AED 25bn, debt falling, dividend covered ~2x; **IAS 24 election leaves most government-ecosystem RPTs unquantified (biggest deduction)**; **founder-MD Alabbar chairs a competing developer**; thin board independence (2 of ~11); Dubai Creek Harbour AED 7.5bn related-party purchase (2022); RERA guarantees AED 9.0bn; Emaar-India litigation; CFO change; cash-conversion improved to ~370 days; **not a serial acquirer** (§24 Filter 4 not tripped). |

## 2. New Red Flags

**Severity is INVERTED — higher = worse.** Only evidence-supported items not already prominent above.

| Red Flag | Why It Matters | Evidence | Severity /100 *(higher = worse)* |
|---|---|---|---:|
| **Minority-interest (NCI) leakage — ~21% of consolidated net profit is not owned by Emaar shareholders** | Every consolidated headline the synthesizer will reach for — revenue AED 49.6bn, EBITDA ~AED 24–25bn, net profit AED 22.3bn — **overstates what belongs to the parent's owners.** Owners of the parent get AED 17,599m; non-controlling interests get **AED 4,726m (21.2%)** of FY2025 net profit. Yet NCI is only **AED 13,398m of AED 107,676m total equity (12.4%)** — the minority-held units earn **above-group returns**, so outside holders take a disproportionate slice, and that slice sits mostly in the **separately-listed cyclical developer (Emaar Development) and Emaar Misr** — i.e. the exact peak-flattered earnings. A valuation that puts an EV/EBITDA multiple on *consolidated* EBITDA (ciq_facts TEV/EBITDA 4.0x) silently prices ~21% of EBITDA the parent does not own; the real multiple on owned earnings is higher. Parent EPS (AED 1.99) is already NCI-clean, but EV/EBITDA, revenue and EBITDA are not. | FY2025 AR (IFRS), Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss — profit attribution: net profit 22,325,535; owners of parent 17,599,179; NCI **4,726,356** (2024: 17,449,073 / 13,513,938 / 3,935,135). NCI equity 13,398,290; total equity 107,676m [FY2025 AR, Statement of Financial Position / Changes in Equity; group summary table]. Listed minority subs declare their own dividends [CIQ Key Developments, 2026-02-12 (Emaar Development AED 1.00/sh); 2026-02-23 (Emaar Misr)]. | 52 |

He owns only 2,700,500 Emaar shares (~0.03%), so alignment is reputational, not economic, and no succession plan is disclosed. Eagle Hills acquisition [CIQ Key Developments, 2026-01-30]. CFO change [CIQ Key Developments, 2026-05-22]. | 45 |
| **Syria — deepening *solo* exposure and sanctions/country tail** | Emaar is **removing its JV partner to operate alone** in "The Eighth Gate," a USD 500m mixed-use development in Yafour, near Damascus (via Emaar Syria LTD), announced May 2026. Absolute exposure is small, but taking **full, unhedged principal in a jurisdiction only just emerging from comprehensive US/EU sanctions** is a reputational and secondary-sanctions tail for a BBB+/Baa1 issuer that funds in USD markets and markets to global buyers/banks. International bookings are growing (AED 9.3bn of property sales), so this is a rising, not shrinking, edge exposure. Not named by upstream (external-dependency treated geopolitics only in the aggregate). | CIQ Key Developments, 2026-05-18 (exit of JV structure, Eighth Gate, USD 500m, Damascus); FY2025 AR (IFRS), subsidiaries note — "Emaar Syria LTD"; international sales [Q4 2025 Earnings Press Release, 12-Feb-2026]. | 33 |

**Checked and cleared — not flagged (so the synthesizer knows they were tested):** **Pension/OPEB** immaterial (UAE end-of-service net liability AED 197.9m, ~0.1% of assets; AED 50m annual cost) [CIQ Financials_Annual → Pension/OPEB, FY2025]. **Cybersecurity** disclosed and clean — "No data breaches reported during the year," ISO 27001:2022 certification, penetration testing/red-teaming [FY2025 AR, Responsible Value Creation, p. governance section]. **Supplier concentration** none at group level — the CIQ "Suppliers" file is a relationships list (Otis, Ahluwalia, JLL, intra-group), not a concentration [CIQ Suppliers export]. **One-off earnings boosts immaterial** — gain on sale of JV AED 99m + EEC dilution profit AED 95m + Albro remeasurement ~AED 237m ≈ AED 0.43bn, under 2% of AED 25.7bn PBT; FY2025 was, if anything, *depressed* by a AED 260m FX loss (vs a AED 505m gain in FY2024) [FY2025 AR, Note 8; Note 16]. **Forward tax step-up** is real but already owned upstream — effective rate rose 7.68%→12.98% and stays below the 15% Pillar-Two floor only because of FY2025 transition relief, so margins face a further ~2pp drag as it rolls off [FY2025 AR, Note 9], but external-dependency (DMTT charge) and business-quality (one-off cushion) already carry it.

## 3. Most Severe New Flag

**Minority-interest leakage (severity 52).** It is the largest genuinely-uncovered item and the one that most directly distorts the numbers synthesis and valuation will use. Roughly **one in every five dirhams of consolidated profit — AED 4.7bn of AED 22.3bn — belongs to outside shareholders, not to Emaar Properties owners**, and because the minority-held businesses (the separately-listed Emaar Development and Emaar Misr) run at higher returns than the wholly-owned assets, the leakage (12% of equity but 21% of profit) is concentrated in exactly the cyclical developer earnings that are already peak-flattered. The fix is simple once flagged — value the parent on its ~79% share of EBITDA and earnings, deduct the minority claim in any EV build, and do not read consolidated EV/EBITDA of 4.0x as the multiple on *owned* cash flows — but if the synthesizer carries consolidated figures unadjusted it will overstate what the equity actually owns by about a fifth. It is fully disclosed and not deteriorating, so it is a valuation-accuracy flag, not a governance red flag — but it must not be averaged away.

## 4. Cross-Cutting Patterns

Individually minor, three items rhyme into one pattern: **maximum capital being committed into new Dubai supply at the top of the cycle, of which the owner keeps only ~79%.** (1) An **AED 200bn single-district masterplan** (4.5m sqm GFA) was announced Jun 2026, on top of a guided ~AED 65bn 5-year capex and AED 120bn of gross-development-value land bought in 2025 at market prices — pro-cyclical deployment (2) into a record-supply market (648 launches, 167,000+ units) where consensus already models **−14.8% long-term growth**, (3) while ~21% of the resulting (peak-flattered) profit leaks to minorities. The second, ownership-side thread — government control just re-shuffled (ICD → Emirates Power / Dubai Holding), most government-ecosystem related-party dealings left unquantified under IAS 24, a founder-MD running a live competitor, and a fresh CFO change — is largely owned by capital-allocation, but the **new Eagle Hills competition and the NCI leakage plug into it**: the minority holder is asked to fund a pro-cyclical land-and-build cycle, keep four-fifths of a peaked return, and trust an owner and a founder whose competing interests are only partly visible. None of this is a disqualifier; together it argues for anchoring returns to mid-cycle and adjusting headline economics to the parent's real ownership before any rating.

## earnings — module synthesis

_Source: `earnings/99_earnings-synthesis.md`_

# Earnings Module — EMAR (Synthesis)

*Emaar Properties PJSC (DFM: EMAAR). Dubai/UAE build-to-sell developer (~80%) plus a smaller mall/hotel annuity (~20%). Reporting basis IFRS; currency AED millions unless stated (the dirham is pegged to the US dollar at ~3.6725 AED/USD; company releases state USD equivalents). Fiscal year ends 31 December. Latest reported period: Q1 2026 (quarter ended 31 Mar 2026, released 11 May 2026); next release Q2 2026 on 10 Aug 2026. **This is a re-run (2026-07-16) triggered by an upstream business-model refresh** — `business-model/10_external-dependency.md` and `business-model/99_business-model-synthesis.md` were regenerated, changing the external-dependency risk score from 63 to 62/100 and flagging a net-cash basis discrepancy across modules. The nine earnings specialist outputs (00–08) are unchanged since 2026-07-13 and were re-read in full; the refreshed business-model synthesis was also re-read in full. This synthesis reconciles both sets; it does not re-read the raw pool. Plain-English terms on first use: **backlog** = value of signed sales not yet booked as revenue; **pre-sales** = new sales contracts signed in the period (a leading indicator, not yet revenue); **POC** = revenue booked in step with construction progress on already-sold homes; **EBITDA** = rough operating cash profit before interest, tax and depreciation; **CFO** = cash from operations; **FCF** = CFO − capital spending; **DMTT** = the OECD 15% minimum corporate tax; **bps** = basis points (100 bps = 1.0 percentage point).*

## Abstract

Emaar's reported earnings are accelerating hard — revenue up ~33% on a clean trailing-year basis and EPS up ~31% — but the drivers point two ways, so the setup is mixed rather than durably accelerating. The single engine is Real Estate backlog conversion: a record AED 163.4bn contracted, ~94%-sold backlog locks in three-to-four years of rising recognized revenue. The near-term consensus bar is beatable, yet it sits inside a Dubai property cycle at its peak whose leading indicators are already cooling (pre-sales +16%, backlog growth +39%→+29%, consensus long-term growth −14.8%). The biggest risk is a clean profit beat meeting a sell-off as demand rolls over. Earnings are cash-backed and clean; no verbatim transcript caps clarity. This refresh confirms the read is unchanged: the business-model update was a scoring correction and a net-cash reconciliation note, not a change in Dubai-cycle substance. Verdict: mixed.

## 1. Earnings Verdict

- **Verdict: Mixed earnings setup** — near-term accelerating and beatable (backlog-fed, reported P&L rising, bar reset lower), medium-term decelerating (leading indicators cooling off a cycle peak, development gross margin compressing, multi-year consensus sliding). The two clocks conflict, which is what makes this Mixed rather than "accelerating." This is a **sector-cycle / externally-driven** setup (CLAUDE.md §14), not company-specific durable acceleration. Unchanged by this refresh.
- **Earnings quality /100:** **81** *(from 06 — cash-backed, repeatable, minimal adjustments; bottom of the top band)*
- **Consensus setup /100 (higher = more beatable):** **60** *(synthesis judgment: 04 rates the near-term bar "Low"/beatable and 05 "favors beat," but the multi-year slide, narrowing beat magnitude and live Q2 revenue-timing miss keep it out of the "strong" zone; NOT capped for absence — consensus is present and current)*
- **Earnings volatility /100 (higher = WORSE — inverted):** **52** *(from 07 — material sensitivity; a geared claim on the Dubai cycle, buffered near-term by backlog + net cash; confidence Low)*
- **Next-quarter setup:** **Favors beat** *(from 05 — on the profit line, EPS/EBITDA, specifically; single-quarter revenue can still miss on POC timing)*
- **Biggest earnings driver (one line):** Real Estate backlog conversion — the pace at which the record AED 163.4bn contracted, ~94%-sold backlog is recognized as revenue via percentage-of-completion; near-term direction Improving as deliveries ramp 2026–28 [02 §7; Q1 2026 press release, 11 May 2026].
- **Biggest earnings risk (one line):** "Good print, bad signal" — a clean, backlog-fed profit beat meeting a sell-off as the Dubai cycle rolls over: pre-sales +16% and cooling, backlog growth decelerating +39%→+29%, consensus long-term growth −14.8%, with development gross margin fading off a cycle high (63%→55%, guided "low 50s") [08 #5, #7; 02 §3; 03 §8; 04 §7].
- **Red-flag severity verdict (from 08, verbatim):** **Material concerns.**
- **Cross-module note (this refresh):** the business-model external-dependency risk score moved 63→62/100 (a stale-reference correction, not a substantive change — see Section 3) and a net-cash basis discrepancy across modules was reconciled (Section 3, 5b). Neither changes any earnings score or the verdict.

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation *(CLAUDE.md §8; fix F37)*

- **Strongest bear point:** The "good print, bad signal" trap — Emaar's reported P&L lags demand by 1–4 years through the backlog, so it can keep printing beats while the variables that actually set the stock and forward estimates roll over: pre-sales +16% and cooling, backlog growth +39%→+29%, consensus long-term growth −14.8%, and out-year estimates that imply an earnings peak ~2029 then decline [08 #5, #7; 02 §3; 04 §4–5, §7].
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** The near-term earnings are genuinely visible AND genuinely cash-backed — the AED 163.4bn contracted, ~94%-sold backlog locks in ~3–4 years of rising recognized revenue; earnings quality is 81/100 with normalized CFO/EBITDA of 94% LTM, clean audits, negligible stock comp and no non-GAAP engineering; the bar was reset ~9–16% lower and front-end revisions turned back up in the last 30 days; Emaar beat in 4 of 5 years and 3 of 4 quarters [06 §1–2, §9; 02 §7; 04 §4, §6; 05 §8].
- **Single killer risk (earnings quality + beat/miss):** Development gross margin fading faster than the guided "low 50s" (bull +100 bps capped vs bear −300 bps open) at the same time as a Q2 revenue-timing miss — the profit-beat mechanism breaking in the seasonally soft quarter that missed both lines a year ago (Q2-25: revenue −4.6%, EPS −5.0%) [03 §8; 05 §3, §6; 07 §6].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible (not "none"):** Multi-year consensus is sliding under the low near-term bar — 7 target-price cuts in 3 months, FY2027+ EPS falling each month, LT growth flipped +6% → −14.8% [04 §4–5]. And clean-TTM CFO grew only +3.8% against earnings +31–33% — cash-conversion growth is already decelerating as the customer-advance tailwind plateaus [06 §6; 01 §2].

## 3. Reconciliation

The specialists agree on the numbers (every output reconciles to `ciq_facts.json`); the disagreements are framing/clock differences plus two cross-module items surfaced by this refresh, all resolved conservatively below.

1. **Margins "Stable" (01) vs development gross margin "DOWN" (03).** Reconciled — both are true at different levels: EBITDA (~49%) and EBIT (~45%) margins held flat for three years *only because* SG&A and D&A operating leverage offset a compressing gross margin (57.4%→54.9% FY24→25, guided to "low 50s"). 03 is the more granular, more forward read; the "stable" headline masks the gross-margin fade. Conservative view: treat the operating margin as at a cycle peak with a downward gross-margin bias.
2. **Revenue "Accelerating" (02) vs "Decelerating" (04 / 10).** Reconciled on two clocks: recognized revenue (backlog conversion) is rising and highly visible for ~3–4 years, while the demand that refills the backlog (pre-sales, off-plan bookings) is decelerating off a record 2025. The risk is reading the first as the whole story. This split is exactly why the synthesis verdict is **Mixed**, not "accelerating."
3. **Net cash "~AED 25bn" (broad, CIQ, Mar-26) vs "~net-flat" (strict, CIQ, Mar-26) vs "AED 61.7bn" (broad, company FY2025 Annual Report, Dec-25) — three figures now in play, reconciled.** Within this module, 01 already showed both an internal broad basis (+24,969) and a strict basis (roughly net-flat), noting a FY2024–26 cash/term-deposit reclassification. The refreshed business-model `10_external-dependency.md` (and `99_business-model-synthesis.md` §3) separately cites the company's own FY2025 Annual Report Financial Review (p.13, at 31 Dec 2025): cash and short-term deposits AED 71.5bn − total debt AED 9.8bn = net cash AED 61.7bn — also labelled "broad basis," but evidently netting in a wider pool of short-term deposits than the CIQ export, and at an earlier date (Dec-25) than this module's Mar-26 figures. **Reconciled view (conservative default, CLAUDE.md §4):** consistent with business-model 99 §3's own resolution, this synthesis continues to anchor the earnings-specific leverage read (Section 5b) on the lower, CIQ-sourced ~AED 25bn broad / roughly net-flat strict framing, and flags the company AR's AED 61.7bn figure as a magnitude question for a balance-sheet-focused module to resolve directly against Note 10 of the audited financial statements — not an earnings-quality or solvency concern. All three bases agree directionally (large net cash, no leverage risk); none changes Section 5b's conclusion that neither trigger fires. Freely deployable firepower is smaller than any of the "net cash" headlines because ~AED 43bn of escrow cash is RERA-restricted.
4. **External-dependency risk score: 63 vs 62/100 — a stale reference, not a live disagreement.** `02_revenue-drivers.md` (dated 2026-07-13, pre-refresh) cites "10_external-dependency (score 63/100, 'mostly externally driven')" when agreeing on cycle position. The refreshed `10_external-dependency.md` and `99_business-model-synthesis.md` (both 2026-07-16) state 62/100 as the current figure; business-model 99 §3 attributes the difference to a stale citation elsewhere in its own module (its `12_red-flags-sweep.md`), not a substantive change — the underlying read (Dubai demand/policy/regulation/geopolitics all High; financial-market sensitivities immaterial) is unchanged between versions. **Reconciled view:** 62/100 is the current source of record; this is a business-model score, not an earnings-module score, so it does not alter any earnings verdict score — noted here only because 02 cites the pre-refresh number.
5. **Red-flag verdict vs synthesis verdict — consistent, no conflict.** 08's "Material concerns" and its steer ("near-term beatable but medium-term decelerating — not durable acceleration") align with this synthesis's **Mixed earnings setup**. There is no contradiction to adjudicate; the red-flag review sharpened, not opposed, the verdict.

*No material number-level disagreement between the earnings specialists. The two cross-module items surfaced by the business-model refresh (net-cash basis, external-dependency score) are reconciled above and change no earnings-module score or the verdict.*

## 5. Earnings Setup Summary

### Revenue Setup
The next-12-month revenue trajectory is sustainable and largely insulated from a demand slowdown, because it is the mechanical conversion of a *contracted* AED 163.4bn backlog (~94% already sold) — not a one-time effect: there is no revenue-driving M&A, the AED peg neutralizes FX (93% UAE), and no policy/subsidy inflates the top line (the UAE tax items hit profit, not revenue). The single factor that would flip revenue direction is a sustained roll-over in Dubai off-plan demand that stops replenishing the backlog — but with a ~2–3 year lag, so it threatens 2027+ more than the next year; nearer term, only a construction/handover slippage would slow recognition. The gap between the two stories is explicit and large: recognized revenue is rising ~28–40% while the leading indicators that feed it are decelerating (pre-sales +16%, backlog growth +39%→+29%) — a read that agrees with the refreshed business-model external-dependency classification ("mostly externally driven," 62/100) with no divergence. Reported growth is fully organic — no reported-vs-organic distortion to unwind.

### Margin Setup
Current margins are at or near a Dubai-cycle peak, not a through-cycle run-rate: the development gross margin is flattered by cheap legacy land (carried at AED 50,235m cost) sold at peak prices, a spread management is already guiding down to "low 50s." The driver that takes the largest bite if it moves adversely by 10–20% is that same development gross margin — it drives 80% of revenue, and a faster fade off the cycle high (bear −300 bps vs bull +100 bps, i.e. downside-skewed) drags consolidated margin more than any other single lever; construction input-cost inflation compounds it because there is no cost-escalator on the sold backlog. On margin protection, Emaar is largely a price-taker on the development engine's input costs (inflation is absorbed on fixed-price sold units and passed forward only at the next launch); the partial structural cushions are the ~15% leasing annuity (~69% segment margin, stable) and net finance income on the cash pile — but the latter is rate-sensitive and fading as rates fall, and its absolute size differs depending on which net-cash basis is used (Section 3).

### Quality Check
The single largest gap between reported and economic earnings is on the cash line, not the P&L: reported FCF of AED 31.0bn LTM overstates steady-state cash by ~27% versus normalized operating FCF of ~AED 22.6bn, because the customer-advance build (~AED 8.3bn/yr) and the corporate-tax payment lag (~AED 2.5bn/yr) are both cyclical tailwinds — and this gap is set to *narrow adversely* when Dubai sales cool (normalized CFO/EBITDA has already eased from ~115% in FY23 to ~94% LTM). The GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridge is unusually clean: there is no adjusted EPS, negligible stock comp, and investment property held at cost (no fair-value gains) — the only non-GAAP measure is company-defined EBITDA (folds in finance income), which is definitional and reconciles transparently. To model normalized earnings, start from **GAAP** (audited IFRS EPS AED 1.99, already net of minorities); the P&L needs no scrub — only the reported cash-flow headline needs a haircut toward the normalized level.

### Consensus Bar
For the company to beat materially, the development gross margin has to hold mid-50s and net finance income has to keep lifting the profit line while backlog recognition runs ahead of the soft-Q2 bar — the exact mechanism Q1-26 already demonstrated (EPS +9.6% on a revenue miss). The bar is most likely mis-set at the two ends: the near-term FQ2/FY2026 profit bar looks set too low after the 3-month cut (beatable), while the out-year bar is the fragile part — it rests on a single analyst and a −14.8% long-term-growth read that is either too pessimistic or an early correct call on the cycle turn. A meaningful slice of the near-term bar is anchored to a record-2025 Dubai cycle and to two reversible below-EBIT tailwinds (rate-sensitive finance income; narrowing legacy-land margins); if Dubai demand rolls over, the whole anchor shifts and the "beatable" near-term read does not extend to the multi-year picture.

## 5b. Leverage & Capital Structure

Leverage is within normal range and did not change materially during the period — no dedicated treatment required. *(Neither trigger fires under any of the three net-cash bases now in view: net debt/EBITDA is −0.99x on the CIQ broad basis (net cash AED 24,969m, Mar-26) and roughly net-flat on the CIQ strict basis, both well below the 3.0x Trigger A; the company's own FY2025 Annual Report broad figure (net cash AED 61.7bn, Dec-25, per the refreshed business-model `10_external-dependency.md`) is even more net-cash-positive and does not change the conclusion. Total debt is only AED 10,064m with ~52x interest cover, and the balance sheet moved further into net cash year-over-year on every basis, so no Trigger B change either. Note carried from Section 3: freely deployable firepower is smaller than any of the "net cash" headlines because ~AED 43bn of escrow cash is RERA-restricted and a term-deposit reclassification leaves the CIQ strict basis roughly flat — a firepower nuance, not a leverage risk [ciq_facts net_debt/total_debt/interest_coverage; 01 §1; business-model/10_external-dependency §1, §3].)*

## 6. Key Numbers

- **Revenue growth rate:** FY2025 +39.6% (AED 49,557m); clean TTM +33.4%; Q1-26 +22.8% YoY [01 §1–3].
- **EBITDA margin:** 48.7% FY2025 (CIQ standardized); held ~49% for three years; company non-IFRS EBITDA ~AED 25.6bn (folds in finance income) [01 §1, §4; 03 §3].
- **EPS:** AED 1.99 FY2025 (audited IFRS, basic & diluted); AED 2.14 LTM Mar-26 [01 §1; FY2025 AR Note 29].
- **CFO / EBITDA:** 139% FY2025 headline; **94–105% normalized** (ex customer-advance build) — cash-backed even after the haircut [06 §1–2].
- **Biggest driver current level:** revenue backlog AED 163.4bn Mar-26 (+29% YoY, ~94% of the under-construction pipeline sold) [02 §7; Q1 2026 press release].
- **Consensus gap (present):** FY2026 EPS-norm reset 2.32→1.95 (≈ flat vs FY2025's 1.99, i.e. consensus already bakes a sharp deceleration + the new 9% UAE tax); FY2026 revenue AED 53.1bn [04 §4].
- **Estimate revision direction:** near-term (FQ2/FY26) turned UP last 30 days (+2–3%) after a 3-month cut; multi-year (FY2027+) still sliding; LT growth −14.8%; 7 target-price cuts in 3 months [04 §4–5].
- **Earnings volatility score:** 52/100 (inverted — higher = worse; "material sensitivity"), confidence Low [07 §7].
- **Cross-module note (this refresh):** external-dependency risk 62/100 (was 63/100 in a stale citation, corrected; Section 3); net cash cited across three bases (AED 25.0bn CIQ broad Mar-26 / roughly net-flat CIQ strict Mar-26 / AED 61.7bn company AR broad Dec-25) — all directionally net-cash, no leverage implication (Section 5b).

## 7. What Would Change The Earnings Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Upgrade It | What Would Downgrade It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mixed earnings setup** (near-term accelerating/beatable, medium-term decelerating) | Q2 2026 (10 Aug) shows pre-sales growth holding ≥+16% and backlog growth stops decelerating (stabilizes ≥+29% YoY); development gross margin holds mid-50s; multi-year consensus stops sliding and out-year coverage deepens confirming durable growth — would move toward **Earnings stable/accelerating** | Pre-sales / backlog growth steps down toward flat/negative; development gross margin fades faster than "low 50s"; a Q2 revenue-timing miss lands alongside decelerating leading indicators; multi-year consensus keeps sliding (more target cuts, out-year EPS lower) — would move toward **Earnings decelerating / inflecting — negative** (driver: Dubai off-plan demand roll-over) | Verbatim earnings-call transcript (tone/candor, guidance nuance); group ASP / units-sold (to split reversible price from durable volume); deeper FY2027+ analyst coverage (out-year rests on 1 analyst); the 10 Aug 2026 Q2 pre-sales & backlog-growth print (the first tell of a cycle turn); resolution of the AED 25bn vs AED 61.7bn net-cash figures against Note 10 (a firepower precision item, not a verdict driver) |

*Constraint check: consensus setup is NOT "Unknown" (current CIQ estimates present), so the verdict is not forced off "accelerating" on that ground — but the six High red flags and the decelerating leading indicators / sliding multi-year consensus make **Mixed** the accurate and conservative call. "Earnings accelerating" would overstate durability (08 flag #7, High). This refresh's cross-module reconciliations (Section 3) do not change this constraint check.*

## 8. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Red-flag severity verdict (08, verbatim): Material concerns.** Reported verbatim per instruction; not softened.
- **Dominant trend and driver:** reported earnings are accelerating on backlog conversion (the single engine, ~80% of revenue), but the demand that refills the backlog is decelerating off a record-2025 Dubai peak — so the module read is "near-term up, medium-term down," i.e. Mixed. Classify as a **sector-cycle / externally-driven** thesis (CLAUDE.md §14), not company-specific durable acceleration.
- **Earnings are clean and cash-backed:** the accounting is genuinely clean (no adjusted-EPS engineering, negligible stock comp, investment property at cost, hard-to-fake accruals moving the right way, clean audits) and cash-backed even after stripping the advance tailwind. The catch is not the P&L — it is the reported cash headline, which must be haircut ~27% to a normalized ~AED 22.6bn before it is extrapolated.
- **Consensus bar:** beatable on the profit line for the next 1–2 quarters (bar reset lower and stopped falling, strong beat history) — but that "low bar" wraps a medium-term downgrade (multi-year EPS sliding, 7 target cuts, out-year peak ~2029 then decline). Carry the caveat; do not treat it as a clean beatable bar.
- **Next-quarter & second-quarter look-ahead:** Q2 2026 (10 Aug) favors a profit-line beat against a reset bar, but a single-quarter revenue miss on POC timing is live in exactly the seasonally soft quarter that missed both lines a year ago. FQ3 2026 (~Nov) is slightly harder — it laps a Q3-25 base flattered by a one-off MD120 tax reversal, so repeating the EPS-beat magnitude is tougher even with revenue supported.
- **Top sensitivity variable and direction:** near-term, the pace of Real Estate revenue recognition (Improving — 2026–28 delivery ramp); medium-term, Dubai off-plan demand ("the whole game," Improving but decelerating at a cycle peak). Low near-term sensitivity is deferred, not low, risk — the exposure is downside-asymmetric.
- **Biggest risks — every High red flag from 08 (0 Critical, so no Critical to propagate):**
  - **(High) "Good print, bad signal" (#5) — the single most dangerous:** the backlog-fed P&L can beat while the pre-sales / backlog growth that set the stock roll over; a clean Q2 profit beat could still meet a sell-off.
  - **(High) Leading indicators decelerating off a record peak (#1):** pre-sales +16% and cooling; backlog growth +39%→+29%; supply pipeline 648 launches / 167k+ units.
  - **(High) Cycle-peak volumes/returns are not a run-rate (#2):** 2025 was Dubai's strongest year on record; ROIC 4.7%→13.7% is a near-decade high; base rate is boom-bust (2009; 2015–19).
  - **(High) Development gross margin compressing off a cycle high, downside-skewed (#3):** 63%→55%, guided "low 50s"; the profit-beat mechanism is structurally fading.
  - **(High) Multi-year consensus sliding under the low near-term bar (#4):** LT growth −14.8%; FY2027+ EPS falling; 7 target cuts in 3 months.
  - **(High) A geared claim on one uncontrollable variable; downside-asymmetric, levers compound (#6):** margin, tax and operating deleverage all skew down and stack in a downturn.
  - **(High) Narrative — "earnings accelerating" overstates durability; really a Dubai-cycle bet (#7):** label the verdict cyclical/externally-driven.
  - *(The six High flags are ONE root risk in several views — a geared, peak-cycle Dubai developer with a lagging backlog-fed P&L. Do not average any away, and do not count them as independent problems.)*
- **Consolidated vs owner economics:** ~21% of consolidated profit/EBITDA leaks to Emaar Development minorities; parent EPS (AED 1.99) is already NCI-clean, but any EBITDA/revenue-based read of the setup overstates owner economics by ~a fifth — attribute on the ~79% owned share.
- **Partial-data cap applied and what it limits:** transcript role is filled only by a verdict-stripped sell-side proxy → **earnings clarity capped at 70** (driver/guidance colour unverified; management tone/candor not assessable in this module). Earnings-volatility **confidence is Low** (company discloses no sensitivity for its real property-demand exposure). Neither caps the headline scores.
- **Cross-module items from this refresh (surface, do not double-count):** (1) the business-model external-dependency risk score moved from a stale 63/100 citation (in earnings' own `02_revenue-drivers.md`) to the current 62/100 (in the refreshed business-model output) — a citation correction, not a substantive shift in the Dubai-cycle read; (2) a net-cash basis discrepancy exists across modules — this module's CIQ-sourced ~AED 25bn broad / roughly net-flat strict (Mar-26) vs. the company's own FY2025 Annual Report figure of AED 61.7bn broad (Dec-25, cited in the refreshed business-model output) — both directionally net-cash, reconciled conservatively in Section 3, with no leverage-trigger or earnings-verdict impact; the residual open item (resolving the two figures against Note 10) is a balance-sheet-module task, not an earnings one.
- **Biggest missing data point:** the 10 Aug 2026 Q2 pre-sales and backlog-growth lines — the first place a Dubai cycle turn would show, and the tell that separates "durable" from "rear-view mirror." Secondary gaps: verbatim transcript, group ASP/units, out-year analyst depth, and the AED 25bn vs AED 61.7bn net-cash reconciliation against Note 10.
- **What would change the verdict:** see Section 7 — a Q2 print that holds pre-sales ≥+16% and stops the backlog-growth deceleration upgrades it; a step-down in those leading indicators (or a faster margin fade) downgrades it toward decelerating/inflecting-negative.

## 9. Simple Summary

- **Revenue:** up a lot and will keep rising near-term (record AED 163.4bn sold backlog, ~94% locked), but the new sales that feed it are cooling (+16%, backlog growth +39%→+29%).
- **Margins:** at a Dubai-cycle peak and drifting down — development gross margin 63%→55%, guided to "low 50s"; flat EBITDA/EBIT margins only hide the gross-margin fade behind cost leverage.
- **Are earnings clean?** Yes — clean accounting, cash-backed even after a haircut; the only catch is the reported cash figure, which overstates steady-state by ~27%. Model off GAAP EPS.
- **Is the consensus bar beatable?** Near-term, yes (bar reset lower, beats land on the profit line). Multi-year, no — estimates and targets are being cut (LT growth −14.8%).
- **Next quarter (Q2, 10 Aug):** favors a profit beat, but revenue can miss on timing in the soft quarter that missed both lines a year ago.
- **Biggest sensitivity:** recognition pace this year; Dubai off-plan demand two-to-three years out — and the demand risk is downside-asymmetric.
- **Volatility:** material (52/100, inverted) — a geared bet on the Dubai property cycle, buffered near-term by backlog and net cash.
- **Useful for the master synthesizer?** Yes — clear read: near-term beatable, medium-term decelerating, clean earnings, one root risk (a peak-cycle Dubai developer with a lagging P&L). Red-flag verdict: Material concerns. This refresh changes no earnings score or verdict — it corrects one cross-module citation (external-dependency 63→62) and reconciles a net-cash basis question that does not affect leverage or earnings quality.

## earnings / 01_historical-financials.md

_Source: `earnings/01_historical-financials.md`_

# Historical Financials — EMAR (Emaar Properties PJSC, DFM: EMAAR)

**Reporting basis:** IFRS. **Currency:** AED millions unless stated (AED is pegged to the US dollar at ~3.6725 AED/USD; the US$ figures in company press releases use that peg). **Fiscal year:** ends 31 December. **Shares (diluted):** ~8,838.8m [8].

**Two EBITDA definitions appear in this file and are kept apart (§15):** (a) **company-defined EBITDA** (non-IFRS, from press releases) — which *includes* net finance income and Emaar's share of joint-venture/associate results; and (b) **CIQ standardized EBITDA** = operating income + depreciation/amortisation only. Company EBITDA runs ~AED 1.0–1.5bn above CIQ standardized EBITDA. The multi-year and quarterly tables below use **CIQ standardized EBITDA** as the spine because it foots exactly across all 17 quarters and 5 years; the company-reported figure is reconciled in Section 4.

Plain-English glossary (first use): **EBITDA** = rough proxy for operating cash profit before interest, tax and depreciation; **EBIT** = operating profit; **EPS** = profit per share; **CFO** = cash generated from operations; **FCF** = free cash flow = CFO − capital spending (capex); **net debt** = total borrowings − cash; **bps** = basis points (100 bps = 1.0%); **TTM/LTM** = trailing/last twelve months.

Full line-item series from CIQ Financials_Annual (Income Statement / Balance Sheet / Cash Flow) [6]; LTM/Net-debt pins cross-checked to the facts sidecar [8].

\* **LTM Mar-26 "YoY %" is a period overlap** (LTM = Q2-25→Q1-26) vs full-year FY25 (Q1-25→Q4-25) — it is NOT a clean year-on-year and must not be read as deceleration. The clean YoY is the TTM-vs-prior-TTM comparison in Section 2: **+33.4%**.

\*\* **Net-debt basis (§15).** The row shows the **broad** CIQ basis (net cash printed as a negative number), which nets in short-term/liquid investments and trading securities. On the **strict** basis (total debt − cash & equivalents only), the picture is far less net-cash because AED 11–22bn of liquid assets now sit in a separate "short-term investments" line: strict net cash/(debt) = FY2021 **+16,445 (debt)**, FY2022 **+9,937 (debt)**, FY2023 **−1,596 (cash)**, FY2024 **+2,571 (debt)**, FY2025 **+861 (debt)**, LTM Mar-26 **−2,115 (cash)** [6][7]. Strict Net Debt/EBITDA: FY21 2.11x, FY22 1.06x, FY23 −0.11x, FY24 0.15x, FY25 0.04x, LTM −0.08x. The strict series is distorted by a cash / term-deposit reclassification across FY2024–FY2026 (deposits moved from "cash" into "short-term investments"), so the **broad basis is the more comparable read of the underlying trend** — a genuine move from net debt (FY21–22) to a large, growing net-cash position. Both bases are shown so neither is presented bare (§15). The FY2025 audited "cash and cash equivalents" per Note 10 is AED 52,632,912k [1], a still-broader figure that includes restricted escrow deposits; escrow cash (AED 43,338m at Mar-26 [7]) is RERA-mandated and cannot freely repay debt, so it is excluded from both net-debt bases above.

**Trend-column notes.** (i) FY2021 is CIQ-restated (RS) and FY2022–FY2023 balance sheets are CIQ-reclassified (RC) [6]; margin % can fall while *absolute* EBITDA rises — read the two together [8]. (ii) **Gross/EBITDA/EBIT margins = "Volatile / Stable":** margins *stepped up* sharply FY2021→FY2023 (EBITDA margin 28%→54%) as the revenue mix shifted to higher-margin Dubai build-to-sell handovers, then settled — EBITDA margin has held ~49% and EBIT margin ~45% for three straight years (FY2023–LTM), so those are labelled Stable; gross margin gave back ~800bps off the FY2023 peak (63%→55%) and is labelled Volatile. (iii) **Working Capital "Volatile":** CA − CL is dominated by restricted escrow cash and development receivables on the asset side, while most customer advances sit in *non-current* unearned revenue — so this line mainly reflects balance-sheet scaling, not operating tightness or ease; it is not a clean operating-WC signal. (iv) **Capex "Stable":** PP&E capex is small and range-bound (AED 0.5–1.3bn); Emaar's real development outlay flows through operating cash (as development-property inventory) and a separate "purchase of real-estate properties" investing line (~AED 0.9–1.0bn/yr), not through PP&E capex [6].

## 4. Reported vs Adjusted Metrics

Emaar does **not** disclose a formal adjusted-EBITDA or adjusted-EPS reconciliation. IFRS statements carry no EBITDA line; the "EBITDA" Emaar quotes in press releases is a **company-defined non-IFRS** measure. The table separates the company figure, the CIQ standardized figure, and (for EPS) the audited IFRS number.

| Metric | Reported Value | Adjusted / Standardized Value | Adjustment Amount | Adjustment / Difference Reason | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| EBITDA FY2025 | AED 25.6bn (company, non-IFRS) | AED 24,132m (CIQ standardized) | ~+1.5bn (company higher) | Company EBITDA includes net finance income + share of JV/associate results; CIQ std = operating income + D&A only | [4] press release / [6] CIQ IS |
| EBITDA Q1-2026 | AED 7.2bn (company, non-IFRS) | AED 6,198m (CIQ standardized) | ~+1.0bn (company higher) | Same definitional gap (Q1-26: net finance income 518 + JV income 546 ≈ the +1.0bn) | [3] press release / [7] CIQ IS |
| EBIT | Not separately reported by company | AED 22,552m FY25 / 23,521m LTM (CIQ = operating income) | n/a | Company reports EBITDA and profit-before-tax, not an EBIT subtotal | [6] CIQ IS |
| EPS FY2025 | AED 1.99 (audited, basic & diluted, IFRS) | AED 1.27 (CIQ vendor-normalized) | −0.72 (vendor figure lower) | CIQ "normalized" EPS applies a standard tax charge and strips unusual items (asset write-backs, disposal gains) — a **vendor construct, not a company adjustment** | [1] Note 29 / [6] CIQ IS |

The company's non-IFRS EBITDA sits very close to its profit-before-tax (FY25: EBITDA AED 25.6bn vs PBT AED 25.7bn [4]; Q1-26: both AED 7.2bn [3]) because for Emaar net finance income now roughly offsets depreciation and interest. Reported PBT ties to CIQ EBT-incl-unusual (FY25 25,656; Q1-26 7,246 [6][7]). Where a table above needs a single EBITDA series, it uses **CIQ standardized** for internal consistency; the ~AED 1–1.5bn higher company figure is the reconciling item.

## 6. Key Trend Summary

1. **Revenue growth is Accelerating.** After a −10.6% dip in FY2022, revenue grew +7.3% (FY23), +32.7% (FY24) and +39.6% (FY25), reaching AED 49,557m; on a clean trailing-twelve-month basis it is **+33.4%** (Section 2). Revenue and EBITDA have both roughly doubled since FY2022 (revenue 24.9bn→51.9bn LTM; EBITDA 9.3bn→25.2bn LTM), with a record AED 163.4bn presale backlog at Mar-2026 (+29% YoY) providing visibility [3].
2. **Margins Stable after an earlier step-up.** EBITDA margin jumped from 28% (FY21) to ~54% (FY23) as mix shifted to higher-margin Dubai build-to-sell, then settled at ~49% for three years (FY23–LTM); EBIT margin ~45% and gross margin ~55% are likewise steady after giving back ground from the FY23 peak. Direction: **Stable/Expanding, not compressing** — absolute EBITDA keeps rising even as the percentage plateaus.
3. **Material seasonality: Q4 is the quarter that matters** — ~32–33% of annual revenue every year, with Q1/Q2 the soft quarters (~21%). QoQ moves are seasonal; the YoY column is the clean read (every quarter +20% to +54%).
4. **Inflection points (last 5 years):** (i) FY2022 revenue trough/margin step-up as the group consolidated Dubai build-to-sell and the mix richened; (ii) balance sheet inflected from net debt (FY21 broad +16.3bn) to a large, growing **net-cash** position (broad +25.0bn at Mar-26; strict roughly net-flat given a cash/term-deposit reclassification), alongside S&P BBB+ / Moody's Baa1 upgrades noted for 2025 [4]; (iii) a **cash-vs-earnings divergence** in the latest TTM (earnings +31–33%, CFO +3.8%) driven by the swing in customer presale advances — a level worth watching, routed to earnings-quality (06).

# Revenue Drivers — EMAR

*Emaar Properties PJSC (DFM: EMAAR). Dubai/UAE developer; IFRS; currency AED millions unless stated (AED pegged to USD at ~3.6725). Fiscal year ends 31 December. Latest reported period: Q1 2026 (quarter ended 31 Mar 2026). This agent identifies what MOVES revenue, not what revenue was — the levels come from `01_historical-financials`.*

**Upstream / limitations.** `01_historical-financials` present and used. Business-model `03_segment-map` and `10_external-dependency` present and used. **No verbatim earnings-call transcript in the pool** — management driver colour comes from two FAB Securities "Earnings Call Insight" notes (4Q25, 3Q25), used as a **verdict-stripped, unverified sell-side proxy** (Rating/Target/vs-our-estimate stripped per MODULE_RULES); every driver **number** is traced to a primary document (company press release / annual report / CIQ). Quarterly data is available, so QoQ/seasonality is analysed (not "Not available").

Plain-English glossary (first use): **off-plan** = home sold before/during construction, paid in instalments; **POC (percentage-of-completion)** = revenue booked in proportion to construction cost incurred to date ÷ total estimated cost; **backlog** = value of signed sales not yet recognised as revenue; **pre-sales / bookings** = new sales contracts signed in the period (a leading indicator, not yet IFRS revenue); **ASP** = average selling price; **ADR** = average daily hotel room rate; **GLA** = gross leasable area; **pp** = percentage points; **bps** = basis points (100 bps = 1.0%).

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

**Segment decomposition applied — 3 reportable segments from the business-model module** (`03_segment-map.md`, audited FY2025 Note 3). Not a single-segment business (largest segment, Real Estate, is 79.8% — below the 85% line). Segment-level P&L is disclosed (revenue, result, capex, D&A, assets per IFRS 8), so the split below is from filings, not estimated.

FY2025 revenue mix [FY2025 AR, Note 3; CIQ→Segments, annual]:
- **Real Estate** (build-to-sell developer): AED 39,550m — **79.8%**
- **Leasing, Retail & Related** (malls/commercial rent): AED 7,681m — **15.5%**
- **Hospitality** (hotels/leisure/entertainment): AED 2,326m — **4.7%**
- Geography: **UAE AED 46,153m (93%)** / International AED 3,404m (7%) [CIQ→Segments (Geographic)]

*Mapping note:* the company's press-release groupings ("Malls/Retail/Commercial Leasing" AED 6.3bn; "Hospitality/Leisure/Entertainment" AED 4.2bn; "Recurring revenue" AED 10.5bn) are a *different cut* from the 3 audited IFRS segments and do not map 1:1 (leisure/entertainment sits in different buckets). This report uses the IFRS/CIQ 3-segment spine (consistent with `01` and segment-map) and cross-references the company cut where useful [Q4/FY2025 press release, 12 Feb 2026].

## 2. Revenue Driver Tree

| Business Type | Revenue Formula |
|---|---|
| Multi-segment developer + landlord | Sum of segment revenue drivers |
| Real Estate (~80%) — build-to-sell developer | Σ(off-plan units sold × price × % construction completed in period) — recognised over time by POC |
| Leasing/Retail (~15%) — landlord | Leasable area × occupancy × rent per sq m + turnover rent + service charges |
| Hospitality (~5%) | (rooms × occupancy × room rate) + attraction tickets + F&B + hotel-management fees |

**Company-specific one-line formula:**
Reported revenue ≈ **opening sold backlog converted by construction progress (POC) on the ~80% development engine** + **recurring mall rent and hotel income on the ~20% annuity.** The swing factor is the development line, and its revenue this year is *bookings made 1–4 years ago* being recognised as buildings rise — so **reported revenue lags demand.** The true leading indicators are **contracted pre-sales** and the **revenue backlog**, not current-quarter recognised revenue [FY2025 AR, Auditor's Report — Key Audit Matter, revenue recognition; Q1 2026 press release, 11 May 2026].

---

## 3. Market / Share / Price / Mix Split

| Driver Bucket | Current Direction | Evidence | Importance /100 |
|---|---|---|---:|
| End-market demand (Dubai off-plan residential) | Improving now, at/near cycle peak | Dubai 2025 record: >270,000 transactions worth AED 892bn [FAB 4Q25 proxy]; 215,458 residential transactions +18.9% [10_external-dependency]; population passed 4m. But consensus long-term growth −14.8% and a fast-rising supply pipeline (648 launches / 167,000+ units) say the market treats this as a peak | 90 |
| Company market share (primary market) | Stable | Group property sales +16% to AED 80.4bn FY2025; launches 90–100% absorbed [FAB 4Q25 proxy]; but the UAE build-to-sell core (Emaar Development) grew slower, sales +9% [Q4 PR] — Emaar roughly tracked, did not outpace, the market. AED 80.4bn ≈ 9% of the AED 892bn total Dubai transaction value (which includes secondary resale — a rough ratio, not a clean primary-market share) | 70 |
| Price / realization | Improving | Management: launches at "increased prices … no pressure on pricing" [FAB 4Q25 proxy]; Delivered-Homes value +49.6% FY2025 [CIQ→Industry-Specific]. Group ASP is **not disclosed** — the volume-vs-price split cannot be isolated (data gap) | 60 |
| Product / customer / geography mix | Shifting toward development + UAE | Real Estate share rose to 79.8% (FY24 74.7%); recurring (Leasing+Hospitality) share fell to 20.2% (FY24 25.3%) as development outgrew the annuity [CIQ→Segments]; 93% UAE. Villa/apartment mix ~40/60 [FAB 4Q25 proxy]; buyers ~80% first-time, top nationality India 20% [FAB 3Q25 proxy] | 55 |
| FX translation | Stable / immaterial | 93% of revenue is UAE and AED is pegged to USD; only ~7% international (Egypt EGP, India INR) carries translation risk [10_external-dependency; CIQ→Segments (Geographic)] | 10 |
| M&A / divestitures | Negligible to revenue | No revenue-driving acquisition; Emaar Misr (Egypt) already consolidated; Eighth Gate (Syria) JV-exit is tiny [Key-Developments, 18 May 2026]. Large 2026 land moves (AED 200bn masterplan; Emaar Hills AED 100bn 50-50 JV; 36m sq ft, AED 120bn gross development value) are **future pipeline**, not current revenue [Key-Developments, 11 Jun 2026; FAB 3Q25/4Q25 proxy] | 10 |

**This is organic demand, not acquired or FX-driven growth.** FY2025 +39.6% and Q1-26 +23% were UAE development revenue recognised on previously-sold, contracted backlog — no material acquisition or currency contribution (Section 6).

**Cycle-position read (Hard Rule — cyclical/policy-exposed business).** The latest reported period sits **at or near a Dubai property-cycle peak on the leading indicators, with a lagging revenue cushion underneath:**
- *Bookings and demand are at a record (peak signal).* FY2025 was Dubai's strongest year on record; Emaar's property sales hit an all-time high AED 80.4bn; group return on invested capital (ROIC — profit earned per AED of capital) rose to ~13.7% LTM from ~4.7% in FY2021, a near-decade high [ciq_facts multi_year_trajectory]. These are **not a normalised run-rate**; the base rate for Dubai property is boom-bust (2009; the 2015–2019 downturn) [10_external-dependency].
- *Momentum is already decelerating.* Backlog growth slowed from +39% YoY (Dec-25) to +29% (Mar-26); pre-sales growth cooled to +16%; the UAE core grew +9% [Q4 PR; Q1 PR]. Consensus long-term growth is −14.8% and out-year estimates imply an earnings **peak ~2029, then decline** [04_guidance-consensus].
- *But reported revenue has a 3–4 year cushion.* The AED 163.4bn contracted backlog (~3.3× annual revenue; ~94% of the under-construction pipeline already sold) means recognised revenue can keep rising for ~3–4 years even if new sales roll over [Q1 PR; FAB 3Q25 proxy]. So the **near-term revenue driver (backlog conversion) is far more stable than the medium-term driver (new demand).**
- *One-time items.* There is **no one-time policy/subsidy tailwind inflating revenue** — the new UAE Corporate Tax + 15% Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (DMTT), and the Q3-25 MD120 tax relief, are **profit-line** items, not revenue [10_external-dependency; FAB 3Q25 proxy]. The non-run-rate element is the **record-cycle demand backdrop itself**, which sets bookings and therefore future revenue.

This agrees with `10_external-dependency` (score 63/100, "mostly externally driven") — no divergence.

---

## 7. The Single Biggest Revenue Driver

**Real Estate backlog conversion — the pace at which the AED 163.4bn contracted, sold backlog is recognised as revenue via percentage-of-completion (construction/delivery progress on already-sold units).** This is the single biggest lever because Real Estate is ~80% of revenue and its revenue is mechanically the conversion of sold backlog as buildings rise: a 10–20% change in the pace of Real Estate recognition moves total revenue ~8–16%, more than any other driver. Its **current direction is Improving** — backlog is at a record AED 163.4bn (+29% YoY), ~94% of the under-construction pipeline is already sold, and unit deliveries are set to "ramp materially" through 2026–28 [Q1 PR; FAB 4Q25 proxy]. Because the backlog is contracted and covers ~3–4 years of revenue, the **next-12-month revenue is highly visible and biased up**, largely insulated from a demand slowdown.

The one caveat that separates near-term from medium-term: backlog conversion is fed upstream by **new Dubai off-plan pre-sales**, which are at a cyclical record and already decelerating (backlog growth +39%→+29% YoY; consensus long-term growth −14.8%). So the biggest driver of the *next year* (backlog conversion) is safe and rising; the biggest risk to the *medium term* (2027+) is whether Dubai demand keeps replenishing the backlog once today's record cohort is delivered — the classic developer split between a visible, contracted near term and a cycle-exposed out-year.

## earnings / 03_margin-drivers.md
